title: Fold both delta windows through one cohort function, tiled and age-matched

body:
## Summary
Move the cohort fold (total, hired, funnel reach and conversion, time-to-hire sample, source and channel rows) out of the two hand-kept copies in db/analytics.ts into one pure `app/_lib/analytics-cohort.ts`, and derive both windows of the period delta from one captured `now` as half-open, tiling intervals. Two defects close by construction: the prior window's source read stops counting the current window's candidates, and the prior cohort is judged as it stood at its own window end, so the headline hire-rate and time-to-hire chips stop comparing a closed cohort against one still in flight.

## Description
The period-over-period deltas are the Analytics tab's answer to 'is hiring getting better'. Today the two sides of every delta come from two different functions: `pipelineAnalytics` (the live battery) and `pipelineAnalyticsPrior` (the slim prior slice added for performance). Their folds are copies, held together only by a deepEqual test, and that test was written to preserve the full battery's behaviour, including a leak: the source-origin query is lower-bounded only, so the prior window's per-source volume also counts every current-window entry. The test comment calls this 'the exact asymmetry the slim function must reproduce'.

The larger defect is maturity. Both cohorts are evaluated as of now. A candidate created 50 days ago has had 50 days to be hired; one created 10 days ago has had 10. So on any team whose median time-to-hire is near the window length, the hire-rate delta reads as a decline and the time-to-hire delta reads as an improvement, every time, with no change in behaviour. The registry's small-sample-honesty subject names this exactly (state-the-accrual-horizon: 'When a figure is compared across periods, the periods must be equally mature'), and analytics-time-windows' cohort-matched-comparison and half-open-interval-policy techniques give the shape of the fix.

The fix is one fold with an `asOfMs` parameter: a terminal row counts as hired, and joins the time-to-hire sample, only when its terminal transition (stage_changed_at, the same stamp the TTH math already uses) is before asOfMs. The current window passes now, so nothing changes there; the prior passes its own end, so both cohorts have had the same 0..N days to mature. The windows come from one `deltaWindows(now, days)` helper whose prior end IS the current start. Every other analytics module in this context (bottleneck, momentum, offer, forecast, deltas) is already pure and tested in isolation; the cohort fold is the one piece still inside the SQL module, and that is why it could fork.

Funnel stages before the terminal one keep their current-stage basis in the prior slice (a stage-as-of read needs the event ledger). The fold states that in its header, and gating each rate delta on both sides' n stops those legs from turning into alarms on thin cohorts. Coordination: r05 analytics-metrics A/B also edit db/analytics.ts (the target filter and the stage-dwell read, which are different regions). This card's builder rebases on whatever they land and re-reads the file first.

## Flow
1. `app/_lib/analytics-cohort.ts` (pure): `deltaWindows(nowMs, days)` -> half-open { current, prior } sharing one boundary; `foldCohort(rows, axis, { asOfMs })` -> { total, hired, funnel[{stage, reached, current, conversionPct}], tthDays[], avgTimeToHireDays, timeToHireSamples, byChannel }; `foldSources(rows, axis, asOfMs)` for the origin join's rows.
2. db/analytics.ts: pipelineAnalytics calls foldCohort for its cohort scalars (asOf = its endMs); pipelineAnalyticsPrior becomes a SELECT plus foldCohort with asOf = the prior end; the prior source query gains `AND p.created_at < ?`; PriorWindowSlice gains funnel reach and timeToHireSamples.
3. analytics-deltas.ts: its AnalyticsSlice reads reach and samples; hireRatePct, funnel conversion and time-to-hire deltas are gated on both sides at MIN_RATE_DELTA_N, the gate the source and channel rows already use.
4. route.ts: capture now once, call deltaWindows, pass the pair to both reads.
5. analytics-prior-slice.test.ts: the asymmetry assertion becomes a tiling assertion; add the age-matching cases. Map the new module in feature-doc-map.json and record the as-of basis in the analytics README's deltas section.

## Expected impact
The two coloured chips a recruiter reads first stop carrying a built-in bias. On the shipped corpus a 30-day view compares a cohort with at most 30 days to hire against one with up to 60. The per-source movement becomes correct before any surface renders it. One fold means the next figure added to the cohort cannot diverge between the two windows, and the byte-identity test that pinned a leak is replaced by a tiling test that pins the invariant.

## Evaluation
Claim: both sides of every period delta fold through one function over tiled, equally mature windows, and each rate delta is gated on both sides' n.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass.
After: 7 of 7.
Method: gate - node:test cases in analytics-cohort.test.ts, analytics-prior-slice.test.ts and analytics-deltas.test.ts, run under npm run test:unit plus the integration gate.
Result: pending build.
Gate: architecture.

title: Metric pack preview: every thin row says how many more and roughly when
acceptance: accrualHorizon({ have: 5, need: 8, perWeek: 1.5, windowDays: null, nowMs }) -> { more: 3, etaWeeks: 2, etaDate: nowMs + 14 days, reason: null }
accrualHorizon({ have: 5, need: 8, perWeek: 0 or null, ... }) -> { more: 3, etaWeeks: null, etaDate: null, reason: 'no-pace' } - no date is invented when nothing has accrued recently

Sliding window: accrualHorizon({ have: 4, need: 8, perWeek: 1, windowDays: 30 }) -> reason 'window-too-narrow' (steady state is 30/7 x 1 = 4.3 < 8, so a 30-day window never clears at this pace), etaDate null

buildMetricPack with a pace input of 1.5 hires/week and 5 time-to-hire samples: the time_to_hire row carries need { more: 3, unit: 'hires', etaWeeks: 2 }; a measured row carries need: null; recruiter_capacity with 2 open roles carries need { more: 1, unit: 'roles', etaWeeks: null, reason: 'not-accruing' }

renderMetricPack: the caveat line for a thin row states the shortfall and the date or its reason (from the same `need` the JSON carries), so the Markdown attachment and the JSON response cannot disagree

metricPackPreview(pack): blockers (thin / not_measurable) sorted before measured rows; summary { publishable: 2, total: 4 }; earliestClear = the latest blocker ETA, or null when any blocker has no ETA

The pack route derives perWeek from the payload's momentum series (sum of MomentumWeek.hired / weeks) and passes it to buildMetricPack; with no hires in the series, perWeek is 0 and every hire-accrued need reports 'no-pace'
npm run i18n:check passes with the new analytics.metricPack keys in all four catalogs

app/api/analytics/metric-pack/route.ts:196 already returns the pack as JSON (`return NextResponse.json(pack)`) when format is not md, and route.ts:147 already holds the full pipelineAnalytics payload, momentum included - so a preview needs no new store read

app/_lib/metric-pack.ts:262 and messages/en.json:8320 - a thin row's only guidance is 'only {sample} observations. Real, but too thin to publish.' It gives no target (MIN_SAMPLE = 8 at metric-pack.ts:36, 40 actions for hours saved at :223, MIN_OPEN_ROLES = 3 at :40) and no timeline

app/_lib/analytics-momentum.ts:32 - `MomentumWeek` carries a weekly `hired` count and db/analytics.ts:174 exposes `momentum: MomentumWeek[]` on the payload: the hire pace the ETA needs is already computed on every read

app/_lib/metric-pack.ts:193 - the pack can be windowed (`windowDays`). A sliding window's sample does not grow without bound, so an honest horizon also has to say when the window itself is too narrow to ever clear. Nothing states that today

app/features/insights/analytics/sections/PerformanceBriefing.tsx:394-399 - the forecast band already applies half of this idea (it names its floor and the distance to it: 'minHires, hires, minWeeks, weeks'), so a per-claim shortfall is established house copy. What is missing is the date, which the registry's state-the-accrual-horizon technique names: 'A refusal with a date attached is a plan; without one it is an excuse'
rollback: Reverting the series restores the plain download link. accrual-horizon.ts and the preview files are new. metric-pack.ts only gains an optional `need` field and one optional input (`pace`), so existing callers keep compiling. The new catalog keys go out in the same revert commit in all four locales.
runner_up: Judged deltas: each period chip carries both sides' n and a moved / within-noise / thin verdict (a two-proportion interval), so '-12 pts' on 3-of-9 vs 5-of-11 stops painting a coral alarm. Traded because it needs slot A's two-sided n to land first.
body:
## Summary
Replace the metric pack's blind download link with an in-app preview. It shows every row with its status and basis, and for each row that blocks publication it states how many more observations the row needs and, at the workspace's recent hire pace, roughly when it will clear. It also states plainly when the chosen window is too narrow to ever clear at that pace. Download (Markdown) stays one click away. The same `need` figure travels into the Markdown caveats, so the file and the screen say the same thing.

## Description
The metric pack is the artefact a recruiter takes to procurement, and its honesty contract (measured / thin / not measurable, with certifiable only when every row is measured) is careful. On the page it is a plain `<a href>` to a Markdown attachment. The recruiter who needs to know whether they can send it this week has to download, open, find the 'Not publication-ready' block, and then guess. The caveat says 'only 5 observations. Real, but too thin to publish.' It does not say the floor is 8, and it does not say that at 1.5 hires a week that is about two weeks away.

The app already holds every number the answer needs. The pack route already has the full analytics payload, including the weekly momentum series with its hire counts. The route already serves the pack as JSON. The floors are named constants. The forecast band already sets the precedent of naming a floor and the distance to it. The missing piece is the registry's accrual-horizon step 5: compute the count needed, the current rate of accrual and the resulting date, and say so.

The horizon is honest in three ways that a plain 'ETA' would not be. When nothing has accrued recently there is no date, only the shortfall ('no-pace'). When a row does not accrue over time (open roles per recruiter) it says so ('not-accruing'). And a windowed pack's sample is bounded by pace times window, so a 30-day pack on a one-hire-a-week team can never reach 8 hires. The preview says 'widen the window or use all time' instead of promising a date that never comes. The pure `accrual-horizon.ts` is written for reuse. The forecast band's refusal can adopt it next, and that is left out of this write set on purpose.

## Flow
1. `app/_lib/accrual-horizon.ts` (pure): `accrualHorizon({ have, need, perWeek, windowDays, nowMs })` -> { more, etaWeeks, etaDate, reason: null | 'no-pace' | 'window-too-narrow' | 'not-accruing' }.
2. metric-pack.ts: optional input `pace: { hiresPerWeek }`; each non-measured row gets `need` in its own sampling unit (hires / actions / roles / responses); `caveatThin` and `caveatNotMeasurable` gain a need sentence built from the same object.
3. metric-pack/route.ts: derive hiresPerWeek from `analytics.momentum` and pass it in. JSON and Markdown are unchanged otherwise.
4. `metricPackPreview.ts` (pure view model): blockers first, a publishable-count summary, and the earliest date by which every blocker clears, or null.
5. `MetricPackPreview.tsx`: opened from the header button (Modal primitive, PANEL/CHIP recipes, tokens only, both themes). It fetches `/api/analytics/metric-pack?days=` as JSON and offers the Markdown download and the window hint. AnalyticsHeader swaps the `<a>` for the trigger, keeping the role-scope label.
6. Catalog keys for the need sentences, reasons and preview chrome land in en/cs/de/fr in one commit. The analytics README's metric-pack section describes the preview and the horizon rule.

## Expected impact
A recruiter can answer 'can I send this yet, and if not, when?' on the page, without downloading anything. The 'thin' refusal becomes a plan with a date, or an explicit reason why there is none. The window-too-narrow verdict catches the most common self-inflicted thin pack: someone picks 30 days to look current and never clears the floor.

## Evaluation
Claim: the pack preview states, per blocking row, the shortfall and an accrual date or an explicit no-date reason, and the Markdown carries the same statement.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass.
After: 8 of 8.
Method: gate - node:test cases in accrual-horizon.test.ts, metric-pack.test.ts and metricPackPreview.test.ts, plus npm run i18n:check, under the integration gate.
Result: pending build.
Gate: contract.
